newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: The things they said in NZ parliament in 1996.
newsitem.headline: The things they said in NZ parliament in 1996.

text.p: Nick Venter of the New Zealand Press Association reviews what MPs had to say about each other and the world in Parliament this year.
MOST HONEST MP
Mike Moore: I know I said I would take only five minutes, but then again why should I keep my promises? No one else does.
UNDERSTATEMENT OF THE YEAR:
Winston Peters: It's a funny thing how circumstances can change.
QUICKEST CHANGE OF HEART: Richard Prebble to Doug Kidd (barely 24 hours after voting for him as Speaker): You are a disgrace already.
INSINCERE APOLOGIES
Ross Robertson: I apologise for saying the member (Roger Sowry) was a toad.
FACETIOUS POINTS OF ORDER
Phil Goff: I would like to move an extension of time. The minister (John Banks) on his feet has had the opportunity to repeat his notes only four times. I would like to hear them again.
Roger McClay: I raise a point of order Mr Speaker. Would it be out of order for me to call this member (Rick Barker) an irrelevant dork?
MOST GENEROUS MP
Mark Peck: I went out and had a meal just recently and there was 10c change which I offered to the waitress. She gave it back to me.
THE UNSENTIMENTAL
Jill Pettis: That member (Roger Sowry) who just resumed his seat looks as if he has been weaned on a pickle. Sandra Lee on Margaret Austin: An ex-Labour Party bunny hopper.
THE SENTIMENTAL
Roger McClay: I am proud to know that I can call New Zealand's Prime Minister Jim, or the leader of the Labour opposition, Helen. How remarkable that they call me Roger.
THE THINGS NATIONAL MPS SAY WHEN THEY DON'T KNOW WHO THEIR COALITION PARTNER WILL BE

Bill Birch: We know him (Winston Peters) well on this side of the House. We know him very very well. We know his capacity, we know his weaknesses and we know that he spends a lot of time trying to look good on television. We also know that he is a huge risk and anybody who wanted to take that risk would have to be out of his or her mind.
Paul East: For a political party, one needs more than a nice haircut and an Italian suit.
THE THINGS WINSTON PETERS SAID UNDER THE SAME CIRCUMSTANCES

The Prime Minister is not fit for the job and come 12 October he will be out. He should not get on his phone and call me like he did last time, because we are not interested in political, quisling behaviour.
The Prime Minister being the uninformed bucolic hick he is.
MICHAEL CULLEN
On Simon Upton: The National Party member with five School Certificate subjects and therefore its ranking intellectual.
On Jim Bolger: A leader who has raised alzheimer's disease to a political virtue
DAVID LANGE

On the Tokelau Islands penal code: I took a lot of the press gallery there, and discovered on my return, very sadly, that I could have murdered the lot of them for a total fine of about $2800, the maximum penalty for murder at that stage being $200 a head.
On himself: I came here nearly 20 years ago. I was young. I was huge, I was the ultimate product of the welfare state and the ultimate extension of the Plunket graph.

On Bill Birch: I often think of Bill Birch who, when I was ill last year, wrote the most moving personal letter I received in hospital. Yet I have spent a political life portraying him as a heartless, venal, mechanical, robotic, uncaring fiend -- and it did not quite work. Then, of course, we blamed him for everything he did, and he took credit for everything we did. He got his own back in that spectacular fashion.
On Winston Peters: He would have been with us today, would he not, Tau, if he had not been detained by a full-length mirror.
On Graeme Lee: God works in a mysterious way, and if she is feeling good that day, it could be on mate.
